newsitem.title: USA: Black dismisses talk of role in copper selloff.
newsitem.headline: Black dismisses talk of role in copper selloff.

text.p: Canadian copper trader Herbert Black dismissed talk that he played a key role behind Tuesday's big selloff in copper futures.
"I have been out of the market - I covered my shorts last week in the rally," Black said. "I am basically completely flat. I have no position, none whatsoever."
"In fact I'm sick today - I had a short position and I covered it, and it's now down," Black said. "I lost a potential profit."
LME copper prices tumbled $100 on Tuesday, losing five percent of its value. In New York COMEX copper futures were down more than five cents per pound at 91.20 cents midday.
Several traders believed that initial heavy selling Tuesday emanated from Black who owns scrap dealer American Iron & Metal.
London Metal Exchange copper stocks plunged 13,475 tonnes on Tuesday, pushing stocks down to six-year lows, but this failed to prompt any rally.
LME stocks have fallen by more than 100,000 tonnes in the past two months.

"I think people are beginning to realise, which I knew all along but could not take the pain anymore, that all they are doing is moving it from one warehouse to another," Black said. "It has nothing to do with business. It's definitely not being consumed."
Black said there was now more copper in bonded Chinese warehouses and elsewhere off exchange than currently in LME stockpiles which Tuesday fell to 132,350 tonnes.
"Come the weeks ahead, we will see all this stuff being redelivered to the exchanges, and people will come to realise it was all just smoke and mirrors."
Black expected the market to trade sideways for a while. In Tokyo Tuesday, LME chairman Raj Bagri told a news conference there was no evidence at the moment of a squeeze in LME copper stocks.
"These are normal trade movements," Bagri said. "There is no doubt that copper consumption is going extremely well."
